page.layout: One column of text. Above it, a printed ornamental border (not text), then the full-width dedication heading and the title of the letter. The text opens with a woodcut initial R at the left. Below the last line, the gathering signature at the lower right. No margin notes.

main_text.l: AD CHRISTIANISS. FRANCIÆ REGEM HENRICVM II.
Gulielmi Rouillij Epistola.
REGES Dij mortales,
immortalitatem consequi possunt
duabus potissimum rationi-
bus, literarum honore, & ar-
morum gloria. Qua duo aeter-
nitati paranda officia, uni o-
lim Palladi mystice attribu-
ta, post paucos, sed maximos Principes Alexandrum,
Cæsarem, & Carolum Magnum simul sic præstitit, &
ea exercuit felicissima memoria Rex Franciscus
pater tuus (ô Rex Christianissime) ut consum-man-
dam armorum gloriam filio relinquens, literarum ho-
norem ad summum extulerit. Tu vero utrumque sic
es amplexus, ut togata militia decus patri aliquate-
nus concedens, rerum bellicarum victorias, & trium-
phos persequaris, pari nixu iuxtà, atque successu.
Quamobrem cùm huius utriusque laudis memoran-
da exempla ad te, supra cæteros omnes Christianos
Principes referri debeant: hoc ipsum volumen, quod

page.notes: The woodcut initial R (a figure scene within a frame) is joined to the first word as "REGES". The printed text reads "Dij" and "Qua" as shown. Several words are printed with a long s rendered as a plain s, transcribed as such. The signature "Aa 2" is set at the lower right and its final numeral is read as printed. Faint show-through of the reverse page is not transcribed.
